The Under 7.5 at -107 on LowVig carries a 179.8 edge_bps, well above our 100 threshold, beating a median of -115 by a substantial margin. results_picks.reasoning: Jacob deGrom on the mound for Texas is a massive pitching edge over Grayson Rodriguez and the Angels lineup. The spread edge is real at 161 bps — BetRivers offers +112 on the Rangers -1.5 against a median of +105, representing genuine line value on a side backed by arguably the best starter on today's slate. The Angels are a cellar-dweller and deGrom's dominance makes covering 1.5 runs a reasonable ask.

The Braves -1.5 spread at +102 on FanDuel is a standout value with 195 bps of edge over the median of -106 — you are getting plus money on a heavy favorite covering 1.5 runs. Bryce Elder faces Miles Mikolas and the struggling Nationals, and Atlanta's lineup depth makes run-line coverage very attainable at home. The market consensus has Atlanta as a -216 moneyline favorite, making this spread price a clear inefficiency.

The Thunder ML at +115 on Bovada carries 203 bps of edge over the median of +106 — one of the sharpest moneyline values on the entire board today. The market as a whole makes OKC a slight road dog despite the line suggesting a near pick'em game, and getting plus money on what most books imply is roughly a coin flip represents legitimate value. Bovada is the outlier here and this number is worth acting on before it corrects.

Walker Buehler takes the hill for San Diego against Jeffrey Springs and the Athletics — a significant pitching edge at home. BetRivers posts +170 on the Padres -1.5 against a median of +155, generating 218 bps of edge, the largest spread edge on today's entire board. The Padres are -128 to -136 on the ML across books, meaning the run line at +170 is a clear overlay for a team expected to win comfortably.

The Golden Knights +1.5 puck line at -145 on BetMGM has 206 bps of edge over the median of -158, the largest puck line edge in the NHL slate. Colorado is a big favorite at around -195 on the ML, but the puck line at -145 is a meaningful discount for a VGK team capable of keeping this close or winning outright. Playoff hockey is notoriously tight and buying the extra cushion here at a well-priced number is sound value.

Gavin Williams has been solid for Cleveland and faces Cristopher Sanchez in a matchup where the market is giving 192 bps of edge on the Guardians ML at +167 versus a median of +154. The Phillies are installed as big -185 favorites, but the Guardians at +167 represent legitimate underdog value given the pitching matchup is more competitive than the line implies. BetOnline offers the best available number and this qualifies as a strong plus-odds spot.

Chris Bassitt is a quality arm for Baltimore against Jack Flaherty and the Tigers, and the Orioles ML at -125 on LowVig carries 134 bps of edge over the median of -132. LowVig's reduced-juice pricing gives real value here — the true implied probability across the market sits closer to -132, so -125 is a clean entry point. Bassitt's consistency and Baltimore's home advantage make this a straightforward lean at a line with measurable positive edge.

ig_carousel_topic.topic: The Kelly criterion explained without the math degree
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text: You're probably betting the wrong size. Every single game.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors pick flat units or go by gut. 1 unit on everything. Or 3 units when it 'feels strong.' Neither approach is built to grow a bankroll over time.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: Kelly sizes your bet based on your actual edge. Bigger edge, more you stake. Smaller edge, less. The formula keeps you from blowing up on a bad week and lets winners compound over time.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Say your bankroll is $1,000. You find a bet where your model says you win 56% of the time at -110 odds. Full Kelly says bet about 3.7% of your roll, so $37. Quarter Kelly (safer) says $9.25. Small. Deliberate. Repeatable.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: The bettors who last years aren't the ones with the hottest picks. They're the ones who never blow up. Sizing is how you stay in the game long enough for the edge to show up.
